summary: A voter who first backed tougher enforcement softens when it reaches someone he knows who was working.
realLife: In interviews with rural voters, several split people who committed serious crimes from workers supporting families. One farmer accepted removing violent offenders, then regretted her vote after a friend's hardworking father was deported. Another was torn after losing a coworker. A third wanted newcomers to come legally and be amazing citizens, and one saw immigrants as a strain on care, a claim a researcher on the page disputes. Personal ties moved two of the voters.
sources: https://kffhealthnews.org/rural-health/ap-kff-rural-voter-poll-midterms-immigration-crackdown-views-economy/ (AP and KFF Health News report on rural voters' views)
